bc_squamish.blurb: Squamish sits on Howe Sound in coastal British Columbia, where steep granodiorite domes and walls rise almost from sea level beside the town. Trad is the largest share of the climbing, followed by bouldering and then sport, with a small number of ice, mixed and aid lines. Grades cluster from 5.10 to 5.12, backed by a solid layer of 5.7 to 5.9 routes, and the boulder problems run from V0 up through the V7 range with a few harder. Stawamus Chief, the Smoke Bluffs, Murrin Park and Mamquam FSR are the biggest pieces, from big multi-pitch faces to short single-pitch crags and boulder fields. The rock is clean and grippy, with cracks, slabs and bolted faces. Rain is common on this coast, so sunnier, faster-drying crags are useful on damp days.

mt_southwest_region.blurb: Southwest Montana gathers the climbing around Bozeman, Big Sky, Butte and the surrounding ranges, from Paradise Valley in the east to the Madison River and Big Belt Mountains. It is a mixed bag: sport and bouldering are the most plentiful, trad is well represented, and winter brings a real ice and mixed scene, centered on Hyalite Canyon. Most rock climbs fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with a healthy number of easier routes and a handful of harder ones. Rock changes by canyon, with limestone buttresses and gneiss walls the two main types in Gallatin Canyon and other rock elsewhere. Gallatin Canyon, Hyalite, Bear Canyon, Bozeman Pass and the Bridger Range sit close to town, while Spire Rock needs a longer drive. Something is usually in condition in any season.

ca_san_francisco_bay_area.blurb: The Bay Area spreads its climbing over the whole metro region: city boulders in San Francisco, parks around Berkeley and Oakland, the Santa Cruz Mountains to the south, Marin to the north, and the rural hills of the wine counties. Bouldering makes up more than half of the climbing, with sport next, then top-rope and a modest amount of trad. Roped grades mostly run 5.10 to 5.12, with a decent spread of moderates and boulder problems from V0 through the V8 range. Rock varies, including soft sandstone at Mount Diablo and Castle Rock and coastal cliffs in Sonoma. It is mostly a quick-session region, climbable year-round except after rain, with hot inland summers and milder days at the coast.

ca_central_coast.blurb: California's Central Coast runs for roughly 300 miles, from the Santa Monica Mountains up to Monterey. Climbing here is scattered across small crags and boulder fields instead of one big destination. Bouldering is the largest group, then sport and trad, with some top-rope. Most roped routes sit between 5.7 and 5.11, with a decent number at 5.12 and a few harder; boulder problems cover everything from V0 to the double digits. Santa Barbara, the Ojai highway corridor, Pinnacles and San Luis Obispo carry most of the climbs. Much of the rock near Santa Barbara and Ojai is medium sandstone that can be crumbly, while San Luis Obispo has volcanic rock and conglomerate shows up inland. Expect pleasant coastal days, small cliffs and plenty of scenery.

wv_new_river_gorge_the.blurb: The New River Gorge is the largest climbing region in the eastern US, cut through the West Virginia hills around Fayetteville with two more gorges nearby, the Meadow River and the Summersville Lake area. The cliffs are very hard, featured sandstone, mostly 30 to 120 feet tall, offering crack and face climbing with a technical, puzzle-like feel. Sport leads, followed by trad and then bouldering. Routes are overwhelmingly 5.10 to 5.12, with a good number of 5.9 and below and a real top end of 5.13 and 5.14, so it favors strong, experienced climbers. Spring and fall are the prime seasons. Some crags are close to roads, while others are a long walk in.

or_central_oregon.blurb: Central Oregon is the high-desert country around Bend, Redmond and Terrebonne, and one famous park, Smith Rock, holds well over half of its climbing. The Crooked River runs through the gorge there, and the walls are best known for sport routes, with trad and crack lines in the lower canyon. Away from it, Trout Creek offers hexagonal basalt columns for strong crack climbers, while Cline Falls, Meadow Camp and a large bouldering collection round things out. Sport is most common, followed by bouldering and trad. Roped grades are concentrated between 5.10 and 5.12, with a fair showing of moderates and some 5.13 and 5.14. Spring and fall are the best seasons, since summer is hot and winter days are short.
